newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour wants new BOE/Treasury relationship.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour wants new BOE/Treasury relationship.

text.p: Gordon Brown, finance spokesman for Britain's opposition Labour party, said he favoured a new and more formal machinery for relations between the Treasury and the Bank of England.

But he declined to spell out whether a Labour government would make the central bank independent. "The present system of the relationship between the Chancellor and the Governor is inherently unstable. It's based on a personal relationship, it's not based on a formal machinery," Brown told Reuters Financial Television.
"I think people have gradually come to our view that we should set up a monetary policy executive within the Bank of England," he added.

"At the same time we should broaden the membership of the Court of the Bank of England and then we should look at the track record of the Bank of England before we make a final decision about what to do next.
"I want a more formal position for the Bank of England...and we will then make a decision about the issues related to independence."
